ai.description: This small frog reaches 25 mm. It is brown or reddish-brown with a darker dorsal pattern and a pale belly. Key features include a pointed snout and the absence of vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micryletta inornata* is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct dark dorsal pattern, featuring a plain, uniform reddish-brown back compared to the mottled or striped backs of similar microhylids.
ai.habitat: *Micryletta inornata* inhabits leaf litter in tropical evergreen forests and moist deciduous woodlands, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Deli Paddy Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among leaf litter and damp vegetation near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micryletta inornata* is an explosive breeder that lays small clutches of eggs in temporary rain pools, typically during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micryletta inornata* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Assam and Mizoram, inhabiting tropical forests at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Deli Paddy Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like buzzing or trilling call, typically heard from flooded fields and grassy areas during the rainy season.
